![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212195/assets/51ee41eea6dfef1292c68a13a438f43c327639e01452e29998bbe513ac3838ba.png)

A container has the shape of a right circular cone. The height of the container is $20\,\text{in}$ and the diameter at the top of the container is $10\,\text{in}.$ Water in the container is evaporating so that its depth, $h$, is decreasing at a constant rate of $\frac{10}{3}\,\text{in/h}.$ At what rate is the volume of water decreasing when the water depth is $12\,\text{in}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the dimensions of the container. Let's call $H=20\,\text{in}$ the height of the conical container, and $R=\frac{10}{2}=5\,\text{in}$ its radius at the top. These quantities are fixed and do not change with time.

Now, let's consider the water level. We call $h$ the height of the water and $r$ the radius of the cone formed by the water. Both of these quantities, and the water volume $v,$ change with time. In particular, we know that

$$
\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{10}{3}\,\text{in}/\text{h},
$$

and we want to know $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}$ when $h=12\,\text{in}.$

We need to find a relation between $v$ and the variable for which we know the rate of change, which is $h.$ This is given by the formula for the volume of a cone:

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h
$$

Before we differentiate the equation with respect to time, note that $r$ also appears in the formula. So, we need to simplify the formula by writing $r$ in terms of $h.$

Note that the cones formed by the container and the water must be similar. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{r}{h} & =\frac{R}{H} \\ \frac{r}{h} & =\frac{5}{20} \\ r & =\frac{h}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the volume formula as

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {(\frac{h}{4})}^{2}h \\ v & =\frac{1}{48}\pi {h}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we have an equation relating $v$ and $h,$ we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}v & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{48}\pi {h}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{16}\pi {h}^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the rate at which the volume of water in the container is changing when $h=12\,\text{in}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{16}\pi (12)^{2}(-\frac{10}{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =-30\pi \,{\text{in}}^{3}/\text{h}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of water is decreasing at a rate of $30\pi \,{\text{in}}^{3}/\text{h}.$
